transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net advanced broadband technical support, my name is Nathan. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Agent

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 58 Park Avenue, Manchester, M14 5JH, and my security PIN is 8841. My router model is the Hub 5 with WAN IP 82.132.210.45.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Heidi, that confirms your account details. What specific disconnect error code is reported by the Cisco AnyConnect client?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It displays 'The secure VPN connection was terminated by the peer. Reason: DTLS handshake packet fragmentation timeout.' because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are non-VPN internet devices on your home network dropping connection at the same time in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, all our phones and smart TVs stream and browse without any interruptions; it is strictly the corporate enterprise VPN tunnel so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I query your Hub 5 WAN packet encapsulation profile on our regional broadband network gateway across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.text: I am a principal cybersecurity risk consultant for a global investment bank! I am in the middle of executing a mandatory regulatory audit for the Bank of England! Every time this VPN crashes, my secure authentication sessions get invalidated and I lose unsaved audit evidence! I am frantic with stress! Why can't S-Net configure broadband properly for corporate remote workers so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.text: Residential broadband packages are engineered for consumer media consumption rather than dedicated enterprise IPsec encapsulation tunneling in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I do not care about consumer marketing distinctions, Nathan! Tell me how to stop this MTU packet fragmentation so I can finish my audit since we depend heavily on this service for remote working and family communications every day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When enterprise VPNs encapsulate packets inside DTLS or ESP headers, a fifteen-hundred-byte MTU exceeds frame payload limits and triggers packet fragmentation across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What specific adjustment needs to be applied to the Hub 5 router to prevent that fragmentation because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router WAN MTU must be adjusted from fifteen hundred down to fourteen hundred and fifty bytes to ensure your S-Net service operates reliably without unexpected dropped packets or connection faults.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you adjust that MTU setting remotely from your diagnostics terminal right now so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then re-initialize the gateway port and set the MTU to fourteen-fifty right now since we depend heavily on this service for remote working and family communications every day.

transcript.text: Bear with me for two minutes while I push the custom MTU clamping profile to your Hub 5 provisioning file to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Heidi. I have provisioned the fourteen-hundred-and-fifty-byte MTU clamp on your broadband profile to ensure your S-Net service operates reliably without unexpected dropped packets or connection faults.
